metadata.independence_basis: Used only filed governance evidence and in-memory probes; no implementer conversation or unfiled defense was used.

reviewed: secret scanner, path safety, change-scope and environment policies
excluded: product tests, services, API, DB, seed, migration and Git mutation

findings.evidence: In-memory probes confirmed detection of supported credential URI schemes, Bearer, named session cookies, PEM, JWT, common named tokens, secret assignments, Windows/UNC/file/HOME paths, NUL, control ratio and listed magic. The scanner returned no findings for mariadb, rediss, amqp/amqps, ftp/sftp/ssh credential URIs, a fully percent-encoded credential URI, a generic Cookie header, an unlabelled high-entropy token, or text-like MZ and ELF samples. Phase 1.3 fixtures add only Bearer, one PostgreSQL URI, one Windows path and PDF magic cases, while the remediation report claims credential-bearing URI, cookie/session and common binary-magic coverage and security evidence still uses FULL/no-detected scan semantics.
findings.reproduction: From the product root, import scanText, classifyOperationalContent and scanBinaryContent into node memory. Pass synthetic vectors for the omitted schemes, fully percent-encoded PostgreSQL URI, JSON-escaped URI, generic Cookie, opaque 40-byte high-entropy value, MZ and ELF buffers. The omitted classes return empty findings while positive controls return expected findings. Inspect run-governance-fixtures.mjs:205-208 to confirm absent regression cases.
findings.impact: Credentials, cookies, opaque tokens or disguised binaries can enter manifest-covered text while deterministic validation still reports a successful FULL/no-detected scan. This is a material A2-class false negative and Phase 1.3 coverage overclaim, so it blocks the governance commit gate.

findings.evidence: The manifest-covered phase-status records active_remediation_task=GOV-PHASE1-REMEDIATION-2 and session_a2_started=false, while filed evidence contains a formal A2 BLOCKER, a READY_FOR_REVIEW Phase 1.3 remediation task and a READY_FOR_REVIEW A3 task. Both safety gates remain NO-GO, so this has not directly created an unsafe GO.
findings.reproduction: Read phase-status.json and compare it with the A2 security-review metadata/outcome and the Phase 1.3 remediation and A3 task-intent statuses.
findings.impact: Validators, reviewers or approvers treating phase-status as authoritative can misidentify the latest formal review, active remediation and approval chronology, weakening audit integrity.

conditions.condition: Before governance commit approval, canonicalize controlled JSON slash and percent encodings, cover all approved credential URI schemes, and fail closed on generic Cookie/Set-Cookie, unlabelled high-entropy tokens and additional binary magic, or explicitly narrow the security contract.
conditions.completion_criterion: Every omitted vector has a deterministic rejection fixture plus adjacent safe negative fixtures, and the exact-manifest validator rejects all unsafe cases.

conditions.condition: Bind binary/type validation to actual bytes, extension and manifest artifact_type instead of accepting a nonempty artifact_type and a limited magic list.
conditions.completion_criterion: Text-suffixed MZ, ELF, compressed or otherwise mismatched content is rejected while all current 87 valid text artifacts pass.

conditions.condition: Correct A2, active-remediation and A3 values in phase-status. After any candidate change, regenerate the exact manifest and before baseline and obtain independent Security revalidation.
conditions.completion_criterion: Phase state matches filed task/review state and the refreshed exact manifest has no missing, unexpected or hash-drift entries.

decisions_required.question: Approve the minimum mandatory contract for credential URI schemes, encoding canonicalization, Cookie handling and high-entropy token detection. The current HIGH finding cannot be waived while retaining the FULL scan claim.
Confirm whether phase-status remains an authoritative current-state artifact; if so, correct it before freezing a new baseline.

exact_87_file_content_scan.high_entropy_triage: 94 lexical candidates reviewed: 5 recorded hashes, 76 path-like strings, 12 long identifiers/control names and 1 deliberate synthetic Bearer fixture fragment; none was an actual credential.

accepted: relative backslash path normalized to slash
limitations: Validation and use are not atomic.
Windows reparse and TOCTOU coverage is not absolute.
${HOME} is accepted as a relative path ref but separately classified as operational HOME expansion.

dump_and_binary_boundary.statement: M320 metadata records an external textual dump reference and operational-path classification; this neither authorizes nor implies dump-byte inclusion. The exact 87-file byte scan found no dump or binary signature.

environment.profile_constraints: explicit JSON, no dotenv, loopback, PostgreSQL 5433, ntmc_erp_rehearsal_* naming, rehearsal mode, no allowed operations and no secret-like keys

residual_risks: No .env* content was read; OS permissions still do not mechanically deny Agent access to ignored .env files.
The safe profile does not constrain child_process, PowerShell, cmd.exe, arbitrary executables or parent permission overrides.
Pattern scanning cannot prove absence of every novel, fragmented, compressed, renamed or multilayer-encoded secret.
Only M320 governance metadata was reviewed; external contents and global sensitive-data absence were not verified by A3.
External artifact storage, retention and redaction remain uncontrolled.
Canonical path and link checks cannot eliminate every Windows reparse or filesystem TOCTOU race.
Branch protection, CODEOWNERS, required review, CI, remote state and the actual staged commit were not established by this read-only review.
Clean reviewer context is procedurally auditable through fixed run/session identifiers but is not cryptographically proven.
A3 after-baseline, other formal reviewer results and final human approval remain incomplete; this result grants no Session B, commit, merge, release or Migration 320 authority.
